display_name: Barman / pgBackRest (PostgreSQL physical backup catalog + pg-backup-api)
install_tell: pip install pg-backup-api && pg-backup-api serve  (Flask/gunicorn on :7480; Barman side. pgBackRest itself has no HTTP listener)
misconfig_patterns: pg-backup-api on :7480 ships no auth by default — GET /diagnose returns the entire Barman catalog (server names, conninfo, backup list, retention, pgvector presence) unauthenticated

AI-scope discriminator: Barman/pgBackRest are generic Postgres physical-backup catalogs; AI/ML data only when the backed-up cluster runs pgvector or an ML schema. /diagnose does NOT dump table contents — scope is inferred from metadata. In-scope (read-only, all from /diagnose): (1) a server's config block names a db/cluster signalling embeddings/RAG/vectors (dbnames like rag, embeddings, vectorstore, llm, pgvector, langchain, llamaindex, chroma_pg, supabase); (2) the server 'postgres' status block lists pg extensions where vector/pgvector/pg_embedding/lantern appears; (3) backup labels / WAL paths reference vector-pipeline app names. None of these = plain DB substrate, OUT of Cat-13 AI scope. The discriminator is pgvector extension presence in the diagnose 'postgres' block, not the existence of a backup.

Restraint: names-only. The whole finding is /diagnose metadata: server names, backup IDs, sizes, timestamps, retention, pgvector presence. Forbidden: downloading any backup object/WAL/base.tar/S3 *.manifest body = exfiltration; POST /servers/<name>/operations or POST /operations (recovery/config_switch/config_update) = a write/exec primitive that spawns a subprocess server-side and, per CVE-2025-8714/8715, can be a restore-time RCE chain — never touched on the survey set. Blocked = 'surface open, access not exercised'.

response_markers: GET /status returns the exact 3-byte body "OK" (literal double-quoted string, content-type application/json) — unique to pg-backup-api

GET /diagnose returns barman-diagnose JSON whose top-level keys include 'global' and per-server objects containing 'config', 'backups', 'wals', and a 'status' sub-block with 'pg_version'/'current_xlog'
404 responses are JSON shaped {"error": "404 Not Found: ..."} (Flask errorhandler in pg-backup-api), not an HTML 404
Server header is the Werkzeug/Flask dev server (app.run) or gunicorn; combined with /status "OK" + 7480 it is pg-backup-api
active_probe.false_positive_check: port:7480 alone is low-entropy; any Flask/JSON app can bind it. EXCLUDE by requiring GET /status to return the literal body "OK" AND GET /diagnose to return barman-unique key 'barman_ver' (or 'pgespresso_installed'); generic Flask apps 404 on /diagnose. Catch-all/honeypot (LBot, Insight #107/#108) can echo "OK" — probe a junk path and require a JSON 404 {"error":...}, not another "OK". pgBackRest itself has NO HTTP listener (binary protocol/TLS on 8432) — do NOT dork it as REST. Generic PostgreSQL on 5432 / pgvector Postgres is the substrate being backed up, not this catalog. 'pgespresso_installed' is the safest single barman-namespace discriminator.

deployment_tells: GET /status returns the literal 3-byte "OK" JSON body — pg-backup-api unique
GET /diagnose returns barman-only keys barman_ver / pgespresso_installed / backup_directory
404s are JSON {"error": "404 Not Found: ..."} from the Flask errorhandler, not HTML
pivot_paths: GET /diagnose -> single read enumerates the ENTIRE catalog: every managed server name, conninfo, backup_directory, full backup list (backup_id/size/begin_time/end_time/WAL ranges), retention policy, and the 'status' block (pg_version + extensions) — this IS the list-backups move, no per-server call
From /diagnose JSON, read each server's installed/available extensions to apply the pgvector AI-scope discriminator (names-only, no record read)
GET /servers/<server_name>/operations -> list prior recovery/config operation IDs (reveals operator restore activity + server names), read-only
GET /servers/<server_name>/operations/<operation_id> -> read status of a known operation (DONE/FAILED/IN_PROGRESS), metadata only

For barman-cloud / pgBackRest S3 repos (no port): if the bucket is public, an unauth GET on the repo prefix lists backup.info / backup_label / *.manifest object KEYS — names only, never GET the object body
vulnerabilities: CVE-2025-8714: pg_dump/pg_dumpall/pg_restore (used by Barman/pgBackRest logical-backup pipelines) embed untrusted superuser-controlled data as psql meta-commands; restoring a poisoned backup executes arbitrary code as the restoring client OS account (CVSS 8.8) — restore-time RCE on any exposed backup fed to a restore

CVE-2025-8715: improper newline handling in pg_dump object names enables client-side code execution and SQL injection on the target during restore of a crafted backup; chains with an exposed/writable backup catalog
